title: Concise order-three tensors over any field have asymptotic subrank at least the cube root of their smallest dimension
difficulty: The argument relates maximal ranks in different slice directions through simultaneous polynomially generic column selections. Conciseness forces the product of each pair of slice-span ranks to dominate the remaining dimension. A third tensor power restricts to a matrix-multiplication tensor whose asymptotic subrank transfers those pairwise bounds back to the original tensor.

title: Sufficiently narrow concise order-three tensors over any field have maximal asymptotic subrank equal to their fixed third dimension
difficulty: The proof restricts a bounded-dimensional matrix space to simultaneously diagonal submatrices and converts large maximal rank into a uniform minimum-rank bound. It proves supermultiplicativity and controls mixed tensor powers even when some restricted factors vanish. Chernoff counting supplies exponentially many independent high-minimum-rank slices, and an explicit diagonal-unit extraction turns them into maximal asymptotic subrank.

title: On connected periodic planar graphs, sufficiently dense zeros force positive-weighted harmonic functions to vanish in inner balls
difficulty: The proof uses planar noncrossing of positive and negative level components to bound the proportion of zeros on a contour. Effective-conductance reductions remove finite bridge and double-edge obstructions in the dual graph. A sparse-nonzero boundary selection and a carefully constructed surrounding cycle then force a contradiction between harmonic maximum principles and the planar contour bound.
